content.comment_body: Hello! I'm facing an unusual issue with the [product_name] module. It's connected to a Mean Well MDR 24V/1.7A power supply. After switching the power off and then back on following a 10-15 minute interval, the module fails to start—none of its LEDs light up. If I reconnect the module to the power supply without powering off the supply (using the module’s terminal), it sometimes starts, but not consistently. If I power cycle the supply with 10-second intervals, it usually starts after three attempts. What might be causing this? Is the problem with the power supply or the [product_name] module?
In this situation, I'd recommend opening a Support Request.

Could you confirm the setting on your Mean Well power supply? These typically include an adjustment to modify the output voltage by 10%. The minimum could be around 21.6V (90% of 24VDC), and I'm not sure if this might make the [product_name] unit stop functioning properly. Is the power supply new? Does it provide a stable output voltage?

I've attempted to set the voltage between 23-25V, but the result remains unchanged. The power supply is new and has been in use for two months; it’s also powering a MikroTik router. I also tried using an ABB AE/S4.1.1.3 power supply, with the same outcome. As a temporary solution, I connected the [product_name] module through a relay output of KNX. Yesterday, after a power loss and 90-minute recovery, I powered the module off and on every 5 seconds. After several tries, the module went online.
I am unable to submit a support request because the product search does not recognize [product_name].
I've located it; it's shown as [product_name] CM EIB.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report inconsistent startup for the [product_name] KNX Communication module after prolonged power-off periods, needing multiple power cycles or direct terminal reconnections to activate the module. This uncertainty about whether the fault is with the module or the power supply disrupts troubleshooting and leads to user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the module to reliably start up after any duration of power loss, without repeated reconnections or power cycling. They also seek clarity on whether the root cause is the module or the power supply.
